messages:
oncall-bot: Pager: high error-rate spike for routing service in eu-west-1 -> spillover to us-central. 5xx misroutes to fallback models. paging on-call: @Maya (primary) @Jesse (secondary) :rotating_light:
Maya: I'm on it, ack. Can someone pull customer impact numbers (calls/sec failing, % of requests rerouted)?
Jesse: grabbing metrics now — running query against routing-metrics in Grafana. short numbers in 1min window: errors went from ~0.1% -> 8.2%. affected customers: a subset of EU prod keys (p-*) showing increased latency + 5xx.
Ravi: pasting first log snippet from routing-proxy (eu-west-1) at 2026-06-12T14:02:12Z:
```
[2026-06-12T14:02:12.124Z] req_id=abcd123 route=eu-west-1 target=us-central fallback=true status=502 err="incompatible-model-variant"
[2026-06-12T14:02:12.129Z] req_id=abce124 route=eu-west-1 target=us-central fallback=true status=502 err="kvcache-miss-length-mismatch"
[2026-06-12T14:02:13.001Z] req_id=abcf125 route=eu-west-1 target=us-central fallback=true status=200 latency_ms=312
```
Jesse: timeline? I see a spike starting 14:01:45Z, correlated with a routing-policy rollout at 14:00:58Z (canary id rp-2026-06-12-14).
Kai: that rollout touched the regional spillover threshold parameter (spill_threshold_pct) -> lowered from 30 to 10 in canary. suspect that aggressive threshold caused earlier spillover.
Hannah: also saw on model side a gated rollout of q4-compat quantized models in us-central around same time (model-rollout mr-q4-2026-06). possible mismatch: newer quantized model doesn't accept certain KV cache shapes from eu sequences -> returns 502 and routes further.
Maya: OK hypotheses to track in-thread: H1: routing policy change lowered threshold -> premature spillover to remote region. H2: fallback model variant incompatibility (quantization + KV shape) causing 502s. H3: autoscaler/backpressure in eu caused re-routes. We should capture logs, traces, and config diffs.
Jesse: pulling policy config diffs from git: `git show origin/main:configs/routing/policies.json@rp-2026-06-12-14` -> shows "spill_threshold_pct": 10 vs previous 30. saving snapshot.
Ravi: dumping route traces (tracer service) for a failed request:
```
trace_id=tr-0ff1
span1 routing-proxy eu-west-1 -> choose fallback cluster us-central (policy=spillover)
span2 transport -> connect (established)
span3 model-server us-central -> init kv-cache (error: shape mismatch)
span4 model-server -> return 502
```
Maya: mitigation path proposals: M1: revert routing policy to previous threshold (immediate). M2: restrict cross-region spillover to opt-in only (short term). M3: revert the quantized model rollout in us-central. Which is fastest?
Kai: M1 is fastest (config rollback), M3 requires model deploy rollback and QA. we should do M1 now + M3 if errors persist.
Maya: Jesse, can you run the rollback of the canary config (rp-2026-06-12-14)? I'll coordinate with deploy. Use runbook: https://redwood.company/runbooks/routing-failover -> step "policy-rollback"
Jesse: running `infractl config rollback --service routing --canary rp-2026-06-12-14` now.
deploy-bot: infractl: rollback job started (job id rb-9876). ETA ~20s.
Maya: cutting a temporary rule to block eu -> us spillover as hotfix too. adding `region_affinity_enforce: true` to eu-west-1 routing context.
Ravi: pushing rule change now. `routingctl set --region eu-west-1 --affinity enforce` -> applied.
deploy-bot: rollback rb-9876 completed. config now at pre-canary state.
oncall-bot: Alert status: active -> mitigated. error rate in eu-west-1 down to 0.8% in 1m window after changes.
Hannah: we've still seen a handful of 502s tied to model incompatibility from earlier requests; but volume is down significantly. recommend follow-up rollback of model rollout in us-central (mr-q4-2026-06) for safety.
Kai: Agree, open an internal blocking ticket to revert mr-q4-2026-06 and run compatibility tests for kv-cache shapes across regions.
Maya: I'll file RCA doc and assign owners. Quick customer impact note: ~12 customers saw degraded responses for ~9 minutes, estimated 75k token requests affected, majority auto-retried; outreach team notified customers with high error-sla.
Jesse: collected logs bundle and uploaded to /tmp/incidents/1769456789/logbundle.tar.gz and added pointer in case thread: https://internal.storage/redwood/logs/1769456789
Ravi: consolidated timeline draft for RCA:
- 14:00:58Z: routing policy canary rp-2026-06-12-14 applied (spill_threshold_pct 30->10)
- 14:01:20Z: model canary mr-q4-2026-06 begins roll in us-central
- 14:01:45Z: first significant error spike observed in eu-west-1 routing metrics
- 14:02:12Z: failed requests show kvcache shape mismatch -> 502 and further spillover
- 14:03:05Z: mitigation: policy rollback + region affinity enforce applied
- 14:11:00Z: errors back to baseline
Maya: Good. For the RCA doc I'll include hypothesis table: H1 (policy) — high confidence, evidence: config diff + immediate reduction after rollback; H2 (model) — medium confidence, evidence: model-specific 502s and registry rollout timeline; H3 (autoscale) — low confidence, no hotspot on infra CPU/mem.
Hannah: adding logs pointer with model error details:
```
[2026-06-12T14:02:12.129Z] model_id=mr-q4-2026-06 host=us-central-12 err="kvcache shape mismatch: expected 64x128 got 64x127"
[2026-06-12T14:02:12.130Z] model_id=mr-q4-2026-06 host=us-central-12 errstack="panic -> recover -> return 502"
```
Jesse: I've kicked off a ticket to revert mr-q4-2026-06 and added tests: `tests/model/kvshape_compat` to run across eu/us test harness. ticket: RWD-INC-1129.
Maya: linking follow-ups: RCA doc draft https://docs.internal/redwood/rca/1769456789 (owner: Maya), revert-ticket RWD-INC-1129 (owner: Jesse), model-compat investigation (owner: Hannah).
Kai: action items for postmortem: - codify spill_threshold safe bounds, - add pre-rollout compatibility check for kv-cache shapes, - add circuit-breaker to prevent cascading spillover more than X% of requests.
Maya: Thanks all. Marking this thread as the coordination trunk for the RCA assets. I'll tidy timeline and drop final summary once postmortem doc is started. :white_check_mark:
